title: Cyber Security Salary Australia: Hourly to Annual Pay Guide for 2026
description: Convert your cyber security salary Australia hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, super, and award rates for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year, a cyber security professional earning $50 per hour would gross $98,800 annually, with super of $11,856 paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert my cyber security hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, that’s 38 hours per week. For example, $60 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What is the minimum pay rate for cyber security jobs in Australia?
faqs.a: Cyber security roles are typically covered by professional awards or enterprise agreements, so the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) is a floor. Most cyber security salaries are much higher. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for specific awards, but many cyber security positions are above award and negotiated individually.

faqs.q: Does the super guarantee apply to my cyber security salary?
faqs.a: Yes. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if your annual gross is $100,000, your employer adds $12,000 in super. This is not deducted from your salary. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Cyber Security Salary Australia

If you're working in cyber security in Australia, you likely have an hourly rate or a salary offer and want to know what that means across a year, a fortnight, and after tax and super. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year to help you convert your **cyber security salary Australia** into the figures that matter for budgeting and negotiations.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The core calculation is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time work, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly.

Example: A cyber security analyst on $55 per hour working 38 hours per week earns:
- Weekly: $55 × 38 = $2,090
- Fortnightly: $2,090 × 2 = $4,180
- Annual: $55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680

This is your gross pay before tax and before super. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your own hourly rate and toggle casual loading.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Market Rates

Not all cyber security roles are paid the same. The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for award/agreement-free employees, or $33.05 per hour for casuals (including 25% loading). However, cyber security positions are almost always covered by a professional award (such as the Professional Employees Award) or an enterprise agreement, which set higher minimum rates. Many cyber security specialists are also paid above award due to skill shortages.

For a true picture of your **cyber security salary Australia**, check your employment contract or enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, but if you are not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage is the legal floor.

### Casual Loading and Super

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. For example, if the base rate is $50 per hour, the casual rate is $62.50 per hour. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator; instead, add the loading separately. Our [the timesheet](/) has a checkbox for this.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual gross is $120,000, your employer contributes an additional $14,400 to your super fund. This is not part of your take-home pay but is a valuable benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

### Tax on Your Cyber Security Salary

Your gross annual pay is taxed using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a single person earning $108,680, the tax would be approximately $24,667 plus Medicare of $2,174, leaving about $81,839 after tax (excluding HELP or surcharge).

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above: $2,090 per week × 2 = $4,180 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your take-home might be around $3,150 per fortnight (depending on your exact tax situation). Check [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more.

### Why the 38-Hour Week Matters

The 38-hour week is the standard for full-time employees under the National Employment Standards. If your contract says 40 hours, you should use 40 in the formula. But for consistency, this guide and our calculator default to 38 hours. The Australian Bureau of Statistics also uses 38 hours for average weekly earnings calculations.

### What This Guide Doesn't Cover

This estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Final Thoughts on Cyber Security Salary Australia

Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual is essential. Use the formula, check award rates via the Fair Work Ombudsman, and remember that super is on top. For a quick calculation, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your own figures.
